chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith narrated to us in the City of Peace (Baghdad). He said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Rafi' al-Bahili narrated to us. He said: Abu Ghassan al-Masma'i narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us. He said: Imran ibn Jarir narrated to us from al-Hasan. He said: Umar said:
Surely, I have never seen anyone among the people more fitting to lead them to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet than him — meaning, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أحرى: More fitting, worthier, more deserving — superlative denoting highest suitability
key_terms.سنة نبيه: The Sunnah of His Prophet — the prophetic practice and tradition
key_terms.كتاب الله: The Book of Allah — the Quran, primary Islamic scripture
key_terms.يحملهم: To lead them, carry them, bring them — metaphor for guiding and compelling adherence

ai.seo_question: Did Umar ibn al-Khattab testify that Ali ibn Abi Talib was most fitting to lead people to the Quran and Sunnah?
ai.summary: This narration records a remarkable testimony attributed to the second caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab, in which he declares that Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was the most qualified person to guide the Muslim community according to the Quran and the Prophetic Sunnah. The narration is transmitted through a chain of Sunni-connected narrators and preserved in the Amali of Sheikh al-Saduq, demonstrating the cross-traditional recognition of Imam Ali's unique religious authority.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Umar al-Hafith narrated to me in the City of Peace (Baghdad). He said: Muhammad b. `Amr b. Rafi` al-Bahili narrated to us. He said: Abu Ghassan al-Mas`ami narrated to us. He said: `Abd al-Malik b. al-Sabah narrated to us. He said: `Imran b. Jarir narrated to us from al-Hasan. He said: `Umar said:
Surely, I have never seen anyone more fitting to lead the people to the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Prophet than him – meaning, `Ali b. Abi Talib (as).
